title: How Long Is Frozen Food Safe During a Power Outage?

content_html:
With the door kept closed, a full freezer generally holds a safe temperature for about 48 hours and a half-full freezer for about 24 hours. When power returns, decide by temperature and remaining ice crystals, not by smell.

Keep the door closed

Every opening lets warm air in and shortens the safe holding time. Keep food grouped and avoid repeatedly checking it.

Use a thermometer if available

Food that still contains ice crystals or has remained at 40°F (4°C) or below can generally be refrozen or cooked according to official guidance.

Do not taste food to judge safety

Smell, appearance, and taste do not detect every dangerous microorganism. If perishable food was too warm and its history is uncertain, discard it.

Plan ahead for a long outage

Refrigerator/freezer thermometers and ice packs make decisions easier. Dry ice can extend cooling, but it requires ventilation, gloves, and safe handling.
